input: An amine absorption unit was tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln, and the results of the test are reported in this passage. Over a period of 60 days, during which the unit treated gas at a rate of 9 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit succeeded in capturing 90% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. The steam demand associated with the capture was 3.6 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured, while the solvent loss was 1.8 kg per tonne captured. These results are valuable as an indication of what the process can achieve under pilot conditions over a sustained period of 60 days, although it should be borne in mind that beyond 60 days the effect of kiln dust on the solvent remains untested, and so the longer-term behaviour of the solvent in this service is not yet known. The three results are reported together because they describe a single quantity of gas treated in a single run: the proportion of its carbon dioxide that the unit removed, the steam that the removal required, and the solvent that the run consumed, and none of the three figures can properly be detached from the conditions under which the others were obtained.
target:
An amine absorption unit was tested at pilot scale on gas from a cement kiln. Over 60 days at 9 t of carbon dioxide per day, the unit captured 90% of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas. Steam demand was 3.6 gigajoules per tonne of carbon dioxide captured; solvent loss was 1.8 kg per tonne captured.

Capture, steam demand and solvent loss are stated for the same run and the same gas. The capture figure is the share of the carbon dioxide in the treated gas that the unit removed; the steam and solvent figures are stated per tonne captured, so both scale with the quantity the capture figure counts.

The two consumption figures are the operating cost of the capture in physical terms: steam is the energy the separation consumes, and solvent loss is the material it consumes, and both are charged against the same tonne of captured carbon dioxide that the capture figure counts. A change in capture at the same total steam consumption would change the steam figure per tonne without any change in the unit's heat consumption in absolute terms, because the denominator of the figure is the captured quantity.Beyond 60 days, the effect of kiln dust on the solvent is untested. The results describe 60 days of pilot operation on kiln gas, and solvent behaviour over a longer exposure to kiln dust is not established by this test.
